newsitem.title: UK: Fixtures dominate business on sugar freight market.
newsitem.headline: Fixtures dominate business on sugar freight market.

text.p: A number of fixtures emerged on the sugar freight market at the end of the week, including timecharter business, shipbrokers said on Friday.

Fresh inquiry included Gill & Duffus for 13/14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Dunkirk or Calais to Tunisia for April 20/25 and Booker was open for 6,100 tonnes in bulk from St Kitts to UK/Nantes for April 20/28.
Shipbrokers said the most significant fixture of the day came from E D & F Man, which fixed 34/38,000 tonnes for delivery to north Spain to Iran on timecharter.
Man also fixed a bulk voyage trip of 25,000 tonnes from Puerto Quetzal/Acajutla to Casablanca plus options for mid-April dates.
Louis Dreyfus fixed around 23,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to the Black Sea/Baltic, again for mid-April, at a rate reported at $27.00 basis Black Sea.
In other news, the Cypriot-flag bulk carrier Theodoros S. was reported to be offloading its cargo of 20,000 tonnes of raw sugar before docking for repairs following a collision.
Its cargo was being transferred to the Cyprus-flag bulker Spiros C, with the operation expected to take until next week to complete.
